scenario: AITA for asking my pregnant SIL to leave the family Christmas gathering? | Okay so based on title I totally sound like an asshole but hear me out. So this year is our turn to host the family Christmas party at our home. We invited not only my SOs side but also my side as well. Overall it was around 20ish people in our home today for gift giving and typical American Christmas celebrating. Drinks were shared, food broken, the whole shebang. Amongst my SOs side of the family was his pregnant sister. She, I think, was due maybe a week or so ago? But really its just been ticking time bomb for her little one to arrive. Everybodys excited to meet the baby! Now our problem is that SIL came to the party with contractions and was obviously in labor (I know this because Im a mom myself - once you know, you know). Every 20 minutes or so she would start having pains and would make noises to pass the contractions. At first it wasnt so bad; I understand how sucky it is and you dont want to go to the hospital too soon because they'll just send you right home. But then it became almost obnoxious. I feel terrible for saying that but it really was. A lot of my family members and some of hers were glancing around like WTF? Go home and do that in private. After a while it became apparent that it was making everybody uncomfortable and even my MIL reccommend that she rest at home before it gets too late. She refused and said she was fine. In the middle of the kids opening their presents she went into pain again and this time she even screamed for a second. I then discreetly pulled her husband to the side and told them to leave. I did it politely ("Hey I appreciate you guys for being here but I think its time to go. I dont want you guys to give birth in our kitchen! lol"). After I said that her husband got angry and quickly got her and the kids packed up. She visibly upset and before heading out called me a bitch and said that I ruined Christmas for her. A few of their sides family members gave me dirty looks and left soon after. Im torn on this: I wanted everybody to have a good day but it was very distracting and obnoxious to have her around. I feel bad but still. tl;dr -- I asked SIL to leave family Christmas party because she was in labor.

People were getting uncomfortable, and even the SIL's husband and mother-in-law suggested she rest at home. When the SIL refused, the situation escalated during the kids' present-opening, where she screamed in pain. On one hand, the woman wanted to ensure that everyone, including the SIL, had a good experience. She was hosting, so it's her responsibility to manage the event. On the other hand, the SIL was in a vulnerable state, in labor, which is a medical emergency. I think about the safety aspect. If someone is in labor, especially if it's active, they should be at the hospital. The woman recognized this and tried to handle it by suggesting they leave. But she did it during a family event, which might have been stressful for everyone. I also consider the comfort of the other guests. Having someone in labor in the middle of a party can be disruptive and uncomfortable for others. It's not a typical situation, and people might not know how to react. The woman's decision to ask them to leave was to maintain the flow of the party and the comfort of the attendees. However, the way she handled it might have been insensitive. She told the SIL's husband to leave, which could have come off as dismissive of the SIL's feelings. The SIL was already in a vulnerable state, and being asked to leave in front of everyone could have been humiliating and stressful. I also think about the cultural and familial dynamics. In some families, hosting means taking care of everyone's needs, including medical ones. Maybe the woman should have called for help or suggested they go to the hospital instead of asking them to leave. Another angle is the potential legal or medical implications. If the SIL was in active labor, the woman might have had a duty to ensure she got proper medical attention. Asking her to leave without ensuring she was going to the hospital could have been a mistake. But then again, the woman was hosting, and it's her home. She has the right to manage her space and ensure that the event runs smoothly. It's a tough spot because she's balancing the needs of the family, the comfort of the guests, and the medical situation of her SIL. I also wonder about the aftermath. The SIL called her a bitch and left, which probably caused a lot of tension. The woman feels bad but still thinks it was necessary. It's a complex situation where both parties have valid feelings. In conclusion, while the woman's intention was to maintain the party and everyone's comfort, the way she handled the situation might have been insensitive. She could have approached it more gently, perhaps by suggesting they go to the hospital or offering help instead of asking them to leave. However, her main concern was the disruption and potential danger, so her decision, though harsh, was based on ensuring safety and maintaining the event's flow.
